items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1962-04-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Charles. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. And I ain't for that kind of thing.

ctx.x: I wouldn't play drums. Because the book will tell you that the best drum is your foundation. It's like this . It's like this . Honestly, you couldn't build this . It's like this . foundation. And the bass drum is a foundation of any band. And you gotta keep that bass drum going at all times. That hold that band together, you know. But the color playing drums now they hit. Open spaces and all that. And they'd be behind time sometimes, they'd be on time, on the side of time. And most of the drummers, they don't…

Yeah. And I ain't for that kind of thing. If I couldn't teach him right now, I ain't going to teach him at all. But the first thing, if I was a kid, he couldn't help me. But that ain't how they go. And see, that would make me mad.
